rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: The owner edits these words and `plan-seed.mjs` reads them: each block opens with a line of two at-signs and its name, and runs to the next such line.
rules.says: This page's standing text is edited by the owner and read by plan-seed.mjs, each block opening with a line of two at-signs and its name and running to the next such line.

rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: A word in curly braces is filled by the seed at the time of the print: HUB (the full path of the repository the print is for, the working copy and never the live clone), ITEM (the program key)
rules.says: The seed fills each curly-brace word at print time: HUB is the full path of the repository the print is for (the working copy, never the live clone), ITEM the program key, TAKEUP, CLOSE and REVIEW the step numbers, NEXTP, NEXTQ and NEXTL the next free program, found and lesson keys, TRANSCRIPT the transcript path, REVIEWFILE the review's full path, LANDING and TAKEUPLANDING the landing blocks whole (LANDING ends in the pull of the live clone, TAKEUPLANDING pulls nothing).

rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: PUTRIGHT (empty, or in a batch print the paragraph that sets the items of findings whose own text says they were put right to done at the take-up, each with that sentence as what changed)
rules.says: PUTRIGHT is empty, or in a batch print is the paragraph that sets to done at the take-up the items of findings whose own text says they were put right, each with that sentence as what changed.

rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: and in a batch print FINDKEYS (the finding keys of the items the take-up sets to planned), LANDSTEP (the landing step's number, which is also CLOSE)
rules.says: In a batch print the seed also fills FINDKEYS (finding keys of items the take-up sets to planned), LANDSTEP (the landing step's number, also CLOSE), FIRSTGROUP and LASTGROUP (first and last file step), GUARDFILES (files whose plants the landing step runs), LANDEST (landing estimate in minutes) and CHECKS (the seven hub checks as their usage spells them).

rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: and in every print PRICED (the plan's whole number of agent sends: the steps of its Order, one review and two for each round), ORDERN
rules.says: In every print the seed fills PRICED (the whole number of agent sends: the steps of the Order, one review and two for each round), ORDERN (steps of the Order), OVER (two for each round), FILESTEPS (each round's file steps written first to last, rounds joined by 'and') and ROUNDNOTE (empty for one round, otherwise the clause saying each round's steps run together and each later round after the previous round's landing step).

rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: The block take-up-new is the take-up of the single print for work that has no entry (the item switch's value new, with ITEM the next free program key)
rules.says: The take-up-new block is the take-up of the single print for work that has no program entry, used when the item switch's value is new, with ITEM being the next free program key.

rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: and the block landing-round is the landing step of every round of a batch print of several rounds but the last, which leaves the live clone as it is; the last round's landing step is the block landing-step.
rules.says: The landing-round block is the landing step of every round of a multi-round batch print except the last and leaves the live clone as it is, while the last round's landing step is the landing-step block.

rules.heading: # The plan seed's standing text
rules.quote: Nothing above the first block is printed.
rules.says: Text above the first block is never printed into a plan.

rules.heading: @@ take-up
rules.quote: Do: `git status`, read clean; read `PROGRAM.md` whole; run the program command's verb claim with the key of each item the plan names, {ITEM}, and the plan file's path,
rules.says: Take-up Do: read git status clean, read PROGRAM.md whole, then run the program command's claim verb with each named item key and the plan file's path, which sets State to planned and Plan to this plan's first-line title, changes no other field or line and refuses an entry that is not open.

rules.heading: @@ take-up
rules.quote: run the landing command's verb prove for the checks alone, once, its last line read; write the manifest in the session scratchpad with the Write tool, one entry holding a label,
rules.says: Then run the prove verb for the checks alone once and read its last line, write a manifest in the session scratchpad with Write (one entry with a label, a reader-facing subject saying the item is taken up as its one-line message, and PROGRAM.md as its one changed file), run the commit verb on the manifest, then do the take-up landing acts.

rules.heading: @@ take-up
rules.quote: Observe: the entry reads State planned with this plan's title, the report names the key the entry carries wherever it is not the printed one, the verb prove passed,
rules.says: Take-up Observe: the entry reads State planned with this plan's title, the report names a differing entry key, the prove verb passed, the remote's main is the pushed commit with this step's commit above the fetched head, a doctrine gates run exists for it, and status is clean with nothing between the tracking ref and main.

rules.heading: @@ take-up
rules.quote: Kill: a failed stage of the verb prove, met as the rule on a red check gives, ends the step FAILED with its lines;
rules.says: Take-up Kill: a failed prove stage (met as the red-check rule gives) ends it FAILED with its lines; a rebase conflict or push refused as not a fast-forward ends it EJECT with nothing pushed and the rebase ended; a refusal of the verbs or connector by a guard or the harness permission check ends it REFUSED with nothing further done and no other route tried.

rules.heading: @@ take-up
rules.quote: Report `progress/step-{TAKEUP}-report.txt` (new); a send after the first writes its own file, named for the step number, a hyphen, the send's number and -report.txt. Estimate 10 min.
rules.says: The take-up report is written to progress/step-{TAKEUP}-report.txt (new), a later send writing its own file named step number, hyphen, send number, -report.txt, with an estimate of 10 minutes.

rules.heading: Take-up (single print)
rules.quote: Facts: the item is {ITEM} in `PROGRAM.md`, and a seed printed by another session reads an entry whose State is open as work to take;
rules.says: A seed printed by another session reads a program entry whose State is open as work to take, which is why the take-up sets the item to planned and lands it first.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-new
rules.quote: {TAKEUP}. **Taken up: {ITEM} entered in the program as planned with this plan's name and landed, so another session's seed skips it.** Hub, one agent.
rules.says: The take-up-new step is one hub agent that enters work that has no entry into the program as planned with this plan's name and lands it so another session's seed skips it.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-new
rules.quote: the key is read again at the time of use, because another session can take it: before any file is written the step runs `git fetch origin main` and reads the remote's head with `git show origin/main:PROGRAM.md`,
rules.says: Before writing any file the step runs git fetch origin main, reads the remote's PROGRAM.md with git show origin/main:PROGRAM.md and files under the next free key past the larger of the working copy's and the remote's, naming in its report any key differing from the printed one and writing that key wherever the plan names {ITEM} in a file it owns.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-new
rules.quote: the entry is written in the form the plan's section Item entry gives, with every placeholder filled, State planned and Plan this plan's title as written on its first line,
rules.says: The entry is written in the form of the plan's Item entry section with every placeholder filled, State planned and Plan set to the plan's first-line title (written with no phrase the third-person check refuses), ranked after the harness items, and the items count line raised by one.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-new
rules.quote: `PROGRAM.md` passes the Read tool's limit, so it is searched with Grep for its count lines and read with Read at the lines around them;
rules.says: PROGRAM.md exceeds the Read tool's limit, so it is searched with Grep for its count lines and read with Read at the lines around them; the step also leaves the live clone as it is and fetches the remote's main so its commit goes on top.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-new
rules.quote: Do: `git status`, read clean; `git fetch origin main`; `git rebase origin/main`, read as up to date or moved forward; read `PROGRAM.md` at its count lines and its newest entries;
rules.says: Take-up-new Do: git status clean, git fetch origin main, git rebase origin/main read as up to date or forward, read PROGRAM.md at count lines and newest entries, add the entry and raise the items count line changing no other field or line, run prove for the checks alone once, write the manifest (label, subject saying the work is entered and taken up, PROGRAM.md as the one changed file), run the commit verb, then the take-up landing acts.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-new
rules.quote: Observe: the entry stands under the key the report names, reads State planned with this plan's title and holds no placeholder, the items count line is one higher,
rules.says: Take-up-new Observe: the entry stands under the key the report names, reads State planned with the plan's title, holds no placeholder, the items count is one higher, prove passed, remote main is the pushed commit with this commit above the fetched head, a doctrine gates run exists, and status is clean with nothing between tracking ref and main.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-new
rules.quote: Kill: a failed stage of the verb prove, met as the rule on a red check gives, ends the step FAILED with its lines; a conflict in the rebase or a push refused as not a fast-forward
rules.says: Take-up-new Kill: a failed prove stage ends it FAILED; a rebase conflict or non-fast-forward push ends it EJECT with nothing pushed and rebase ended; a refusal of the fetch, rebase, verbs or connector by a guard or harness permission check ends it REFUSED with nothing further done and no other route tried; report progress/step-{TAKEUP}-report.txt (new), estimate 10 min.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-batch
rules.quote: {TAKEUP}. **Taken up: {ITEM} set to planned with this plan's name and landed, so another session's seed skips them.** Hub, one agent.
rules.says: The take-up-batch step is one hub agent that sets the batch's items to planned with this plan's name and lands it so another session's seed skips them.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-batch
rules.quote: the entries are found by their finding keys, {FINDKEYS}; a seed printed by another session reads an entry whose State is open as work to take;
rules.says: The entries are found by their finding keys, and the step names in its report the key each entry carries wherever it differs from the printed one, since another session may land entries between print and rebase.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-batch
rules.quote: the step only claims: it adds no entry, touches no count line, runs no check and leaves the live clone as it is,
rules.says: The batch take-up only claims: it adds no entry, touches no count line, runs no check and leaves the live clone as it is (the landing step brings it forward once when no other step runs); the working copy is clean when it runs and file steps start after it because a rebase needs a clean working copy.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-batch
rules.quote: the plan's title is copied whole into each entry, so the title is written with no phrase the third-person check refuses; `PROGRAM.md` passes the Read tool's limit,
rules.says: The plan's title, copied whole into each entry, contains no phrase the third-person check refuses, and PROGRAM.md is searched with Grep for the keys and read with Read at the lines around each entry.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-batch
rules.quote: Do: `git status`, read clean; `git fetch origin main`; `git rebase origin/main`, read as up to date or moved forward; search `PROGRAM.md` with Grep for the finding keys
rules.says: Take-up-batch Do: git status clean, fetch and rebase onto origin/main, Grep PROGRAM.md for the finding keys and note each entry's key, run the claim verb with the items' keys and plan file path (sets State planned and Plan to the first-line title, changes no other line, refuses a non-open entry), write the manifest (label, message saying the items are taken up, PROGRAM.md the one changed file), run the commit verb, then the take-up landing acts.
rules.enforcer: program.mjs claim verb; plan-land.mjs commit verb

rules.heading: @@ take-up-batch
rules.quote: Observe: the entries read State planned with this plan's title, the report names the key each entry carries wherever it is not the printed one, no other line of the file changed,
rules.says: Take-up-batch Observe: entries read State planned with the plan's title, the report names any differing entry key, no other line changed, remote main is the pushed commit with this commit above the fetched head, a doctrine gates run exists, status clean with nothing between tracking ref and main.

rules.heading: @@ take-up-batch
rules.quote: Kill: an entry of the items that reads other than open ends the step EJECT naming it, with nothing written;
rules.says: Take-up-batch Kill: an item entry not reading open ends it EJECT naming it with nothing written; a rebase conflict or non-fast-forward push ends it EJECT with nothing pushed and rebase ended; a refusal of the fetch, rebase, commit or push by a guard or harness permission check ends it REFUSED with nothing further done and no other route; report progress/step-{TAKEUP}-report.txt (new), estimate 5 min.

rules.heading: Take-up (batch print)
rules.quote: a seed printed by another session reads an entry whose State is open as work to take;
rules.says: A seed printed by another session reads an entry whose State is open as work to take, so the batch take-up must set the items to planned and land before other work.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: {CLOSE}. **Closed in the program, the findings filed, the lesson written where one was learned, the measure recorded, and landed.** Hub, one agent.
rules.says: The close step is one hub agent that closes the item in the program, files the findings, writes any lesson learned, records the measure and lands.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: before any file is written the step runs `git fetch origin main` and reads the remote's head with `git show origin/main:PROGRAM.md`, `git show origin/main:found/` and `git show origin/main:lessons/`,
rules.says: Before writing any file the close step fetches origin main, reads the remote's PROGRAM.md, found/ and lessons/ via git show and files under the next free key past the larger of the working copy's and the remote's, so a commit another session landed does not meet the keys filed.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: the item's key is read from the program at the time of use and not from this plan's text, because the take-up can have found the entry under a later key than the one printed;
rules.says: The item's key is read from the program at the time of use, not from the plan's text, since the take-up may have found it under a later key.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: every Found line of the plan's step reports not marked fixed is a finding and stands only in those reports until it is filed;
rules.says: Every Found line in the plan's step reports not marked fixed is a finding and must be filed.
rules.live_quote: anything found and not fixed, each on a line opening with Found.
rules.missing: That every unfixed Found line is a finding that stands only in the reports until it is filed at the close.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: the measure is the cost instrument's print for this session's transcript at {TRANSCRIPT}, and the instrument prints its figures and the manager records them;
rules.says: The measure is the cost instrument's print for this session's transcript, which prints the figures and the manager records them; and the live-clone pull is the step's last act, when no other step runs, because it changes the gates under every agent.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: Do: read `PROGRAM.md` whole; write the item's state in its entry from the step reports, done where every step in Order handed back DONE and ejected with the finding attached otherwise,
rules.says: Close Do: read PROGRAM.md whole and write the item's state from the step reports, done where every Order step handed back DONE and otherwise ejected with the finding attached, with what changed, by the program command's done verb for a done item.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: for each Found line of the plan's step reports not marked fixed, write the finding as one entry of one JSON file in the session scratchpad with the Write tool,
rules.says: For each unfixed Found line, write one entry of one JSON file in the scratchpad with Write holding its text, the kind of its last line, the files that line names, the sentence after them and the goal and acceptance of its program item, and run the program command's file verb on it, which writes one file in found/ named by its key and adds an open program item ranked after the harness items, raising the items and findings counts, printing each key; the report names each key filed beside the line it came from, key by key and never as a range.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: each file written in the found folder ends, after one empty line, with one line of the finding's own kind, told by its opening words and a colon: Fix in,
rules.says: Each found-folder file ends, after one empty line, with one kind line: 'Fix in:' followed by the names in code spans of the repository's files (guard or page first, four at most), a full stop and one sentence saying the change; or 'Not the repository's' with one sentence saying whose the behaviour is; or, where no file can be told, 'Not placed' with one sentence saying what was searched for.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: for each finding listed in the plan's section Findings passed in, which the owner passed in from another session, add one entry to the same JSON file in the session's own words, filed the same way;
rules.says: For each finding in the plan's Findings passed in section (passed in by the owner from another session), add one entry in the session's own words to the same JSON file and file it the same way.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: where a report carries a line opening Lesson, run the program command's verb lesson with its title, its declaration line and a file in the scratchpad holding its body,
rules.says: Where a report carries a line opening Lesson, run the program command's lesson verb with its title, declaration line and a scratchpad file holding its body, which writes the lesson file under the next number and one index row in LESSONS.md naming number, title and file.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: run the program command's verb measure on the transcript, which runs the cost instrument and writes under the measure item one close entry for this plan
rules.says: Run the program command's measure verb on the transcript, which runs the cost instrument and writes one close entry for the plan under the measure item, every figure copied from the print and no run of seven or more hex-set characters.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: run the landing command's verb prove for the checks alone, once, its last line read; write the manifest in the session scratchpad with the Write tool, one entry for the close
rules.says: Then run prove for the checks alone once reading its last line, write a manifest in the scratchpad with Write (one close entry with a label, a reader-facing one-line message and the close's files), run the commit verb on it, then the landing acts.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: Observe: the entry reads the item's state and what changed, the found folder and the program hold one file and one item for each finding,
rules.says: Close Observe: the entry reads the item's state and what changed, found/ and the program hold one file and item per finding (passed in or found) with counts raised and the report naming each key, the close entry stands under the measure item, each lesson stands with its LESSONS.md index row, prove passed, remote main is the pushed commit, a doctrine gates run exists, the clone's head equals remote main and status is clean.

rules.heading: @@ close-step
rules.quote: Kill: a failed stage of the verb prove, met as the rule on a red check gives, ends the step FAILED with its lines;
rules.says: Close Kill: failed prove stage ends it FAILED; rebase conflict or non-fast-forward push ends it EJECT with nothing pushed and rebase ended; refusal of a verb, fetch, rebase or connector by a guard or the harness permission check ends it REFUSED with nothing further done and no other route tried; an unforeseen shape ends it EJECT naming it; report progress/step-{CLOSE}-report.txt (new), estimate 40 min.

rules.heading: Close step
rules.quote: the remote's main moves under this session, so it is fetched at the time and the plan's commits go on top of it.
rules.says: Because the remote's main moves under the session, the close step fetches it at the time and puts the plan's commits on top of it.

rules.heading: Close step
rules.quote: the next free program key is {NEXTP}, the next free found key is {NEXTQ} and the next lesson number is {NEXTL}, each read when this plan was typed and read again at the time of use, because another session can take one
rules.says: The next free program key, found key and lesson number printed in the plan were read when it was typed and must be read again at the time of use because another session can take one.

rules.heading: @@ review-step
rules.quote: {REVIEW}. **Review.** Hub, one agent per send, Standing. Follow {REVIEWFILE} by that full path for the move the manager notes' unnumbered `Next:` line names, and hand back its verdict line first.
rules.says: The review step is one hub agent per send that follows the review file by its full path for the move the manager notes' unnumbered Next: line names and hands back its verdict line first.

rules.heading: @@ review-step
rules.quote: This step is never a resend: a send of it reads no step's report as its own and does none of any step's Do,
rules.says: The review step is never a resend: a send reads no step's report as its own, does none of any step's Do, and follows the review file from its first line whatever the manager notes say was sent before.

rules.heading: @@ review-step
rules.quote: The review judges that move and does none of it: it does not carry out the Do of the step it judges, runs none of that step's commands, starts no background run,
rules.says: The review judges the move and does none of it: it does not carry out the judged step's Do, runs none of its commands, starts no background run, and writes nothing but its own record in the scratchpad's progress/ folder.
rules.live_quote: You are the checker. You did none of the work you judge, and you change nothing: no edit, no write, no commit, no push.
rules.missing: The review step's own constraints: it does not carry out the judged step's Do, runs none of that step's commands, and writes nothing but its own record in the scratchpad progress/ folder (the checker may write scratch files elsewhere in the scratchpad); the background-run ban is only the general no-unmanaged-process rule.

rules.heading: @@ review-step
rules.quote: Every file, the repository's own files and its git configuration among them, is read with the Read or Grep tool.
rules.says: Every file, including the repository's files and git configuration, is read with Read or Grep.

rules.heading: @@ review-step
rules.quote: The only shell lines are the one `node` command on the review's script under the scratchpad and a single git read the agent rules list;
rules.says: The review's only shell lines are the one node command on the review's script under the scratchpad and a single git read the agent rules list, the git reads being bare (git status, log, show or rev-parse with commit ids and plain flags, no --format or --pretty string, no percent code), each shell line one command with no cd, variable assignment, semicolon, && or pipe.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: The file steps, {FILESTEPS}, run at the same time in the one working copy{ROUNDNOTE}. Each writes only the files its own text names, commits nothing and stages nothing,
rules.says: File steps run at the same time in one working copy; each writes only the files its text names, commits and stages nothing, reads git status as showing changes to its own files and those other file steps own (which it does not touch), and a change it did not make to a file no step owns ends it EJECT naming the file.
rules.live_quote: - When other workers run beside you, stage nothing and commit nothing.
rules.missing: Writing only the files its own text names, reading git status as its own and other file steps' changes, and ending EJECT on a change it did not make to a file no step owns.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: Each edit it makes leaves its file whole, so a run another step starts in that moment reads a file that loads.
rules.says: Each edit a file step makes leaves its file whole, so a concurrent run by another step reads a file that loads.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: It works in this order and no other. First, every edit its findings ask for, its cases and its plants written.
rules.says: A file step works in a fixed order: first every edit its findings ask for, with its cases and plants written.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: Second, for each assertion of a case it wrote or changed, the helper or guard function the assertion calls read with Read and Grep and the assertion checked against that code,
rules.says: Second, for each assertion of a case it wrote or changed, it reads the helper or guard function the assertion calls with Read and Grep, checks the assertion against that code, and puts right any it does not bear out before anything runs.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: Third, the third-person, privacy and quote checks once each, any find in a line the step wrote reworded with no string the code matches changed,
rules.says: Third, run the third-person, privacy and quote checks once each; a find in a line the step wrote is reworded without changing any string the code matches, and a find in another step's file is named in the report and not acted on.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: Fourth, its own cases, each in a run of its own with one case switch to a run, the switch written whole inside double quotes,
rules.says: Fourth, run its own cases, each in its own run with one case switch per run, the switch written whole inside double quotes as "--case=<the case's name>".

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: Fifth, its own new plants, by the plants switch and the switch that names plant keys, followed by those plants' keys joined by commas,
rules.says: Fifth, run its new plants by the plants switch and the plant-keys switch with keys joined by commas copied from the file holding the plant; the run exits 0 whatever it finds, so the step reads each plant's line, strengthens the case in its own file wherever a line says MISSED, and re-runs until every new plant reads CAUGHT and the last line counts none bad and no leak.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: Sixth, the suite's dry listing, the plants switch with its dry switch and the files switch naming the files it edited, made once:
rules.says: Sixth, make the suite's dry listing once (plants switch with its dry switch and the files switch naming the files it edited); a plant listed as stale is re-pointed with Edit where it sits in a file the step owns and run by its key to read CAUGHT, or named in the report with its file and the edit to make where it sits in another step's file, and the listing is not made a second time.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: A red run of a case of its own is met as the rule on a red check gives: the step repairs it once, in a file it wrote in this send,
rules.says: A red run of a file step's own case is repaired once in a file it wrote in this send, and a second red run ends the send FAILED with the report naming the fix.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: A review for a resend of a file step is sent only when no agent is editing the working copy, which is after every file step of the batch has handed back,
rules.says: A review for a resend of a file step is sent only when no agent is editing the working copy, that is after every file step of the batch has handed back, because a review sent during sibling edits judges a moving state.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: Where a step of the batch changed code so that an existing case no longer holds, the landing step puts the code right in the owning step's file and keeps the finding's fix,
rules.says: Where a batch step changed code so an existing case no longer holds, the landing step puts the code right in the owning step's file and keeps the finding's fix, and where the finding asks for the changed behaviour it brings the case to it, never with an assertion that a gate refuses something removed or loosened.

rules.heading: @@ parallel-rules
rules.quote: A suite case never writes into the working copy: a case that needs a program, a found folder, a lessons folder, a plan file, a marker, a repository or a transcript writes it under a temporary folder and removes only that folder.
rules.says: A suite case never writes into the working copy: a case needing a program, found folder, lessons folder, plan file, marker, repository or transcript writes it under a temporary folder and removes only that folder.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: {LANDSTEP}. **Landed once: every edit left for it made first, the dry listing read, every case of the suite run once,
rules.says: The landing step is one hub agent that lands once: makes every left edit first, reads the dry listing, runs every suite case once, runs each edited file's plants, runs the seven checks, makes one commit per file step rebased onto the remote head, closes the wave in the program with findings filed and measure recorded, reruns the checks over the close, pushes once, and pulls the live clone last.
rules.live_quote: Workers that run together stage nothing and commit nothing, and one worker stages and commits after them.
rules.missing: The landing step's dry listing, one commit per file step, the program close with findings filed and measure recorded, rerun of checks over the close, single push and the live-clone pull last (live .claude/skills/landing/SKILL.md covers fetch, rebase, seven checks, suite, push once).

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: Facts: steps {FIRSTGROUP} to {LASTGROUP} left their edits uncommitted in the working copy, each report listing its files, cases and new plants by key,
rules.says: The landing step takes as given that the file steps left uncommitted edits with reports listing files, cases, new plants by key and each stale plant, line or case named for it, and the take-up's commit is already on the remote; the prove verb counts a stale plant its dry listing names as a failure, so a stale plant is moved here before the verb runs; and the plants of every edited file (suite file and each doctrine page among them) are run here.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: an existing case red under the edits is put right here, in the owning step's file where that step changed code so that the case no longer holds and the finding did not ask for the change,
rules.says: An existing case red under the edits is put right in the landing step: in the owning step's file where that step changed code so the case no longer holds and the finding did not ask for the change, or in the case itself where the finding asks for the very behaviour it asserts against, never with an assertion that a gate refuses something removed or loosened, each edit named in the report beside its case and going into the commit of the step whose file or finding it meets.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: a red case or a missed plant is put right at the start of the next send and never after a run in the same send,
rules.says: A red case or missed plant is put right at the start of the next send and never after a run in the same send, except once in a file the step wrote in this send as the red-check rule gives (a missed plant meaning a case asserts too little, strengthened in its case file); a check's find in a file a file step wrote is put right in that file at the start of the next send.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: the stale-plant list comes from the suite's own report before a run, by the plants switch with its dry switch, and not from reading the plants against the edits;
rules.says: The stale-plant list comes from the suite's own report before a run (plants switch with its dry switch) and not from reading plants against the edits; a landing step that edits a gate file runs the whole suite after its last edit and before its first commit.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: the repository's commit hook runs the example, privacy and scope checks at each commit;
rules.says: The repository's commit hook runs the example, privacy and scope checks at each commit; PROGRAM.md passes the Read tool's limit and is read by Grep at its keys and count lines and by Read at the lines around them.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: after this step's code commits are rebased the working copy holds the program and the found folder as the remote's head holds them, so the next free keys,
rules.says: After the code commits are rebased the working copy holds the program and found folder as the remote head holds them, so the next free keys are read from the working copy then, each item's key is read from the program and not the plan's text, and before the close writes any file the step reads the remote head's PROGRAM.md, found/ and lessons/ with git show and files under the next free key past the larger of the working copy's and the remote's.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: the pull of the live clone is this step's last act, when no other step is running, because it changes the gates under every agent;
rules.says: The live clone pull is the landing step's last act, when no other step is running, because it changes the gates under every agent; the measure is the cost instrument's print for this session's transcript.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: Do: read the reports of steps {TAKEUP} to {LASTGROUP} and, in a send after the first, the report of the send before it; `git status`, read as the files steps {FIRSTGROUP} to {LASTGROUP} own changed and nothing else;
rules.says: Landing Do begins by reading the reports of steps from take-up to the last file step (and the previous send's report in a resend), reading git status as showing only the file steps' files changed, and making before any run every edit the reports name for this step (a line in another step's file, a stale plant's re-point, a case of the seed's print among them, and each case holding old behaviour of a changed guard or print brought to the fix).

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: write the manifest in the session scratchpad with the Write tool from the reports, one entry for each of steps {FIRSTGROUP} to {LASTGROUP} in that order,
rules.says: Write the manifest in the scratchpad with Write from the reports, one entry per file step in order, each holding a label, a plain one-line message naming the findings' keys and saying the rest in words, the files changed, the files added and the keys of its new plants (those of a long file among them), an edit made by this step going into the entry of the step whose file it sits in.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: run the landing command's verb prove on the manifest once, which makes the dry listing and the plants run for each file the reports name as changed,
rules.says: Run the prove verb on the manifest once (dry listing, plants for each changed file, the whole suite and the seven checks, with a scratchpad folder after its out switch), read its last line, meet a failed stage as the red-check rule gives, and move a named stale plant with Edit to where its line now stands and run it by key to read CAUGHT.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: run the landing command's verb commit on the manifest, which makes one commit for each of steps {FIRSTGROUP} to {LASTGROUP} in that order and refuses, with nothing committed,
rules.says: Run the commit verb on the manifest, which makes one commit per file step in order and refuses, with nothing committed, a message of more than one line or holding a link, a model's name or a trailer line, a listed file with no change, and a changed file no entry lists.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: `git status`, read clean; `git fetch origin main`; `git rebase origin/main`, and where it stops on a conflict `git rebase --abort` and hand back EJECT naming the files, with nothing pushed;
rules.says: After the commits, read git status clean, fetch origin main and rebase onto it; where the rebase stops on a conflict run git rebase --abort and hand back EJECT naming the files with nothing pushed.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: then the close: read the program's count lines, its newest keys and the found folder's newest key from the working copy, and take the next free keys;
rules.says: Then the close: read the program's count lines, newest keys and the found folder's newest key from the working copy and take the next free keys; run the done verb for the items the take-up set to planned (found by finding key) with what changed and the plan's name, leaving open with its step's reason any item whose finding a report says was not put right.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: write the Found lines of the reports of steps {TAKEUP} to {LASTGROUP} and of this send that are not marked fixed and do not say there is no defect as the entries of one JSON file
rules.says: Write the unfixed Found lines (excluding those saying there is no defect) of the reports from take-up to the last file step and of this send as entries of one scratchpad JSON file, each with text, kind of last line, files named, following sentence and the goal and acceptance of its program item, and run the file verb, which writes one found/ file and one open program item per entry raising items and findings counts, the report naming each filed key beside its source line, key by key and never as a range.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: each file written in the found folder ends, after one empty line, with one line of the finding's own kind, told by its opening words and a colon: Fix in,
rules.says: Each found-folder file ends, after one empty line, with one kind line: 'Fix in' plus the repository's file names in code spans (guard or page first, four at most), a full stop and one sentence on the change; or 'Not the repository's' plus one sentence on whose behaviour it is; or 'Not placed' plus one sentence on what was searched for where no file can be told.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: for each finding listed in the plan's section Findings passed in, which the owner passed in from another session, add one entry to the same JSON file in the session's own words, filed the same way;
rules.says: Each finding in the plan's Findings passed in section gets one entry in the session's own words in the same JSON file, filed the same way; and where a report carries a line opening Lesson the lesson verb is run with title, declaration line and a scratchpad file of its body, writing the lesson file under the next number and one LESSONS.md index row.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: run the program command's verb measure on the transcript, which runs the cost instrument and writes under the measure item one close entry for this plan
rules.says: Run the measure verb on the transcript, writing one close entry under the measure item with every figure copied from the print and no run of seven or more hex-set characters; run prove for the checks alone once reading its last line; add the close entry to the manifest (label, reader-facing one-line message saying the wave is closed and the close's files) and run the commit verb with the close entry's label; then do the landing acts.
rules.enforcer: program.mjs measure verb; plan-land.mjs prove and commit verbs

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: Observe: every stage of the verb prove passed, each stale plant it named caught by key, and the verb prove for the checks alone passed over the close,
rules.says: Landing Observe: every prove stage passed, each stale plant caught by key, checks-alone prove passed over the close, one plain-message commit per file step plus one close commit, items read done or open with a reason, found/ and program hold one file and item per finding with both counts raised, the close entry stands under the measure item, remote main is the pushed commit, a doctrine gates run exists, the clone's head equals remote main, and status is clean with nothing between tracking ref and main.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: Kill: a failed stage of the verb prove, a plant read as MISSED, or a commit the repository's hook refuses,
rules.says: Landing Kill: a failed prove stage, a MISSED plant or a commit the hook refuses (which the red-check rule does not let the step repair, or which stands after its one repair) ends the send FAILED with its lines and nothing written after but report and progress note; a red case whose fix needs a line outside the plan's files or whose cause cannot be read ends it EJECT naming the lines; a conflict the plan's rules do not resolve or a push refused twice ends it EJECT with nothing pushed and rebase ended; a refusal of a command by a guard or harness permission check ends it REFUSED with the refusal's words, nothing further done and no other route tried.

rules.heading: @@ landing-step
rules.quote: Report `progress/step-{LANDSTEP}-report.txt` (new); a send after the first writes its own file, named for the step number, a hyphen, the send's number and -report.txt. Estimate {LANDEST} min.
rules.says: The landing report is written to progress/step-{LANDSTEP}-report.txt (new), a later send writing its own file named step number, hyphen, send number, -report.txt, with the estimate {LANDEST} minutes.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: {LANDSTEP}. **Landed once for its round: every edit left for it made first, the dry listing read, every case of the suite run once,
rules.says: The landing-round step is one hub agent that lands once for its round: makes every left edit first, reads the dry listing, runs every suite case once, runs each edited file's plants, runs the seven checks, makes one commit per round file step rebased onto the remote head, closes the round's items in the program with findings filed, reruns the checks over the close and pushes once with the live clone left as it is.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: the take-up's commit and the commits of every round before this one are on the remote; the verb prove counts a stale plant its dry listing names as a failure,
rules.says: In a round's landing step the take-up commit and every earlier round's commits are already on the remote; the prove verb counts a stale plant its dry listing names as a failure, so a stale plant is moved before the verb runs; and the plants of every edited file (suite file and each doctrine page among them) are run.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: an existing case red under the edits is put right here, in the owning step's file where that step changed code so that the case no longer holds and the finding did not ask for the change,
rules.says: An existing case red under the edits is put right in the round's landing step: in the owning step's file where that step changed code so the case no longer holds and the finding did not ask for it, or in the case itself where the finding asks for the very behaviour asserted against, never with an assertion that a gate refuses something removed or loosened, each edit named in the report beside its case and going into the commit of the step whose file or finding it meets.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: a red case or a missed plant is put right at the start of the next send and never after a run in the same send,
rules.says: A red case or missed plant is put right at the start of the next send, never after a run in the same send, except once in a file the step wrote in this send; a check's find in a file a file step wrote is put right in that file at the start of the next send; the stale-plant list comes from the suite's dry-listing report rather than reading plants against edits; and a landing step that edits a gate file runs the whole suite after its last edit and before its first commit.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: before the close writes any file the step reads the remote's head with `git show origin/main:PROGRAM.md`, `git show origin/main:found/` and `git show origin/main:lessons/`,
rules.says: Before the round's close writes any file the step reads the remote head's PROGRAM.md, found/ and lessons/ and files under the next free key past the larger of the working copy's and the remote's; keys are read from the working copy after the code commits are rebased and each item's key from the program, not the plan's text.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: the live clone is left as it is, because the plan's last landing step brings it forward when no other step is running, and the measure is recorded there and not here;
rules.says: A round's landing step leaves the live clone as it is because the plan's last landing step brings it forward when no other step runs, and the measure is recorded in that last landing step and not in the round's.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: Do: read the reports of steps {TAKEUP} to {LASTGROUP} and, in a send after the first, the report of the send before it;
rules.says: Round landing Do: read the reports from take-up to the round's last file step (and the previous send's report in a resend), read git status as only the round's file steps' files changed, make before any run every edit the reports name for this step, write the manifest in the scratchpad with Write (one entry per file step in order with label, one-line message naming finding keys, changed files, added files and new plant keys), run the prove verb once and read its last line, then run the commit verb, git status clean, fetch and rebase onto origin/main and on a conflict run git rebase --abort and hand back EJECT naming the files with nothing pushed.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: then the close: read the program's count lines, its newest keys and the found folder's newest key from the working copy, and take the next free keys;
rules.says: Then the round's close: take the next free keys, run the done verb for the items the take-up set to planned (leaving open with its step's reason any whose finding was not put right), write the round's unfixed Found lines (excluding those saying there is no defect) as one scratchpad JSON file and run the file verb with each filed key named in the report beside its line and never as a range, give each found-folder file its kind line (Fix in / Not the repository's / Not placed), and run the lesson verb for any Lesson line.
rules.enforcer: program.mjs done, file and lesson verbs

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: for each finding listed in the plan's section Findings passed in, which the owner passed in from another session, add one entry to the same JSON file in the session's own words, filed the same way, in the first round's landing step only;
rules.says: Findings passed in by the owner are added to the filing JSON file in the session's own words and filed the same way in the first round's landing step only.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: run the landing command's verb prove for the checks alone, once, its last line read; add the close entry to the manifest, holding a label, a reader-facing one-line message saying the round is closed
rules.says: Run prove for the checks alone once reading its last line, add the close entry to the manifest (label, reader-facing one-line message saying the round is closed and the close's files), run the commit verb with the close entry's label, then do the take-up landing acts (which pull nothing); the measure verb is not run in a round's landing.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: Observe: every stage of the verb prove passed, each stale plant it named caught by key, and the verb prove for the checks alone passed over the close,
rules.says: Round landing Observe: every prove stage passed, each stale plant caught by key, checks-alone prove passed over the close, one plain-message commit per round file step plus one close commit, items read done or open with a reason, found/ and program hold one file and item per finding with both counts raised, remote main is the pushed commit with those commits above the fetched head, a doctrine gates run exists, and status is clean with nothing between tracking ref and main.

rules.heading: @@ landing-round
rules.quote: Kill: a failed stage of the verb prove, a plant read as MISSED, or a commit the repository's hook refuses,
rules.says: Round landing Kill: a failed prove stage, MISSED plant or hook-refused commit not repaired by the red-check rule ends the send FAILED with its lines; a red case needing a line outside the plan's files or with an unreadable cause ends it EJECT naming the lines; an unresolved conflict or twice-refused push ends it EJECT with nothing pushed and rebase ended; a refusal by a guard or harness permission check ends it REFUSED with the refusal's words and no other route tried; report progress/step-{LANDSTEP}-report.txt (new), estimate {LANDEST} min.
